clue.text: Single chap needs stuff for his flat

parts.note: an unmarried man is a bachelor
to stuff a cushion is to pad it

explanation.surface: An unmarried man must furnish his flat with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' reads as a noun (belongings) but works as the verb meaning fill out.
explanation.definitionFit: A home kept by an unmarried man for entertaining is the classic image of this kind of apartment.

clue.text: Swears yet is not entirely ill-disposed

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the final letter of the word meaning ill-disposed

parts.note: someone ill-disposed to an idea is averse to it

explanation.surface: Someone curses even though they are not wholly hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts the last letter off AVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare solemnly, which is what swearing to something means.

clue.text: Girl growing up on the moors

explanation.surface: A young woman reaching adulthood out on the wild moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name, and also the purple shrub that covers upland moors.

clue.text: Line up, snarling like wolves

indicators.note: snarling suggests the letters of line up are tangled and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A row of wolves stands in line, growling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarling' is used in its sense of tangling, not growling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine is the adjective from the Latin for wolf, meaning wolf-like.

clue.text: Here cars are involved in scientific survey

indicators.note: letters that are involved are wound together, so the letters of here cars get jumbled

explanation.surface: A study of traffic in which local vehicles take part.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic investigation to establish facts is what a scientific survey carries out.

clue.text: A group performing in desert

parts.note: a musical group is a band
a performer is said to be on when on stage

explanation.surface: A music group plays a gig out in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun (sandy waste) but is the verb meaning leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch, walking out on them, is to forsake them.

clue.text: Pound naughty boys — the lads once employed on warships

definitions.text: the lads once employed on warships

parts.note: to pound something into dust is to powder it
mischievous children are called little monkeys

explanation.surface: Thrash the badly behaved lads.
explanation.walkthrough: Boys on old sailing warships carried gunpowder from the magazine to the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Young ship's boys who ferried gunpowder to the cannons in the age of sail had this nickname.

clue.text: Switching to first class suspended

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word class

parts.note: something suspended from a hook is hanging

explanation.surface: Moving up to first class while the service is on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first class' suggests A or travel class; here 'first' simply picks the C from 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering or swapping one thing for another is a synonym of switching.

clue.text: Take charge with ease, say, and call for expropriation

parts.note: to take charge is to command

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the word ease is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: the word ease is pronounced like two letter Es
to call someone on the phone is to ring them

explanation.surface: Seize control effortlessly and demand that property be confiscated.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing property for official use, often by force, is what taking it from its owner by the state means.

clue.text: Work a long time at musical presentation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Labour for ages on a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama set to music and staged with singers is this kind of musical work.

clue.text: Ischia, top resort for nuts

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular answer: the word names a type of nut, so stands for the nuts

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means the letters of Ischia top are sorted again

explanation.surface: Ischia, the best holiday island, for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place (Ischia is an Italian island) but means re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: This green-kernelled seed from a Middle Eastern tree is eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Difficulty with sound production, on day hips dislocated

indicators.note: dislocated means moved out of place, so the letters of on day hips are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical complaint about voice trouble on the day of a hip injury.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the medical term for impairment of the voice, a disorder of speaking.

clue.text: Material for study I'm pursuing

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so I'm comes after the word for study

parts.note: a den is a small private room for study

explanation.surface: Fabric for a study, and I'm after it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Declaration covering wine

parts.note: re means concerning or about, and a piece covering a topic deals with it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A statement with a wine label on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An official statement or account of findings is a formal announcement.

clue.text: Climbing mountains, jokers call for publicity

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the word for mountain is reversed

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain, especially in Switzerland
jokers are playing cards, and a joker person is called a card

explanation.surface: Mountaineering pranksters seek attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' in a down clue turns ALP upwards, giving PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs and posters carried or displayed to advertise something are a form of advertisement.

clue.text: Brief acknowledgement descendant accepted for analysis of verse

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the descendant word holds the short acknowledgement

parts.note: a scion is a descendant of a family
ANS is the short form of answer, and an answer acknowledges a letter

explanation.surface: A quick thank-you from an heir is welcomed by a literary critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief acknowledgement' suggests TA; it is ANS, short for answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the study of a poem's metre, marking stressed and unstressed syllables.

clue.text: Hate a man crudely displaying it

definitions.text: Hate a man crudely displaying it

indicators.note: crudely means roughly put together, so the letters of hate a man are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone shows their loathing of a man in a coarse way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: rough loathing of a man shows the object of curses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or utterly detested, the object of intense loathing.

clue.text: Zero tax is carrying on, gaining tributes

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the word is holds the word on

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being tax-free brings applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds of applause, especially standing ones, are public tributes of praise.

clue.text: Hard lumps of dripping

parts.note: dripping reads as cooking fat, but it is water dripping that freezes into hard spikes

explanation.definitionFit: Hanging spikes of ice form when drips of water freeze as they fall.

clue.text: Place reserved for anyone arriving late

definitions.text: Place reserved for anyone arriving late

parts.words: Place reserved for anyone arriving late
parts.note: seems to describe a seat kept for latecomers, but late here means dead

explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is where dead bodies are kept, and the late are the deceased.

clue.text: Disturbed by poems in books

indicators.note: in means the word for poems goes inside the abbreviation for books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
verse is poetry, a body of poems

explanation.surface: Upset by poetry found in some volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To overset is to upset or overturn, so overset means upset or thrown into disorder.

clue.text: Forces put in the picture

indicators.note: put means placed differently, so the letters of forces are set in another order

explanation.surface: Armed services get briefed on the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in the picture' reads as an idiom for briefing; 'put' alone shuffles FORCES.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall painting done on wet plaster is a kind of painting.

clue.text: Gives Sikh a kitbag holding military-type clothing

indicators.note: holding means the words Sikh a kitbag contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A Sikh soldier is handed a kitbag full of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull brownish-yellow cloth is used for army uniforms.

clue.text: One harassing the folk dwelling between hill-tops

indicators.note: dwelling between means living in the space between, so the folk sit between the two hill-tops

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop on Dartmoor, and the plural gives two of them
the second of the two hilltops
folk are people, men

explanation.surface: Someone bothering the people who live on the moor between the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hill-top, used twice for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who torments others is a persecutor or harasser.

clue.text: Step between the car and the road

definitions.text: between the car and the road

explanation.surface: A pace between a vehicle and the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstep is a tread, and a tyre's grooved surface is the tread touching the road.

clue.text: Off-peak callers?

parts.note: seems to mean people phoning at cheap times, but describes singers calling out from mountain peaks

explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers whose warbling calls echo from mountain tops.

clue.text: Looking severe from the rear

explanation.surface: Seen from behind, someone looks grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and grim-faced, and it is also the back end of a ship.

clue.text: Fool an enemy — start teasing girl with foul-smelling resin

parts.note: an ass is a fool
an is the indefinite article, the letter A
a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of teasing

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Trick your opponent by mocking a young woman who smells of rotten gum.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent gum from giant fennel roots, used in Indian cooking and medicine.
